title: apparatus data-tables are plain double-quoted shell strings, so a literal quote in a note becomes shell and bash -n passes
body:
Two apparatus data-tables hold their rows in a plain double-quoted shell string, so a literal `"` in a note silently turns prose into commands -- and `bash -n` passes.

## What happened

Adding 24 rows to `lib_classify.sh`'s `OVERRIDES` table, two of my notes contained ordinary English quotation marks -- `"a known command that is not implemented yet"` and `D10 ("shell pruned at the cut")`. `OVERRIDES` is a **plain double-quoted string**, so those quotes CLOSED it and the following prose was parsed as shell:

    lib_classify.sh: line 213: known: command not found
    lib_classify.sh: line 291: pruned: command not found

**The table silently lost its rows.** Nothing refused, nothing exited non-zero.

## THREE INSTRUMENTS FAILED IN SEQUENCE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS FILED AS A CLASS

1. **`bash -n` PASSED.** It is a SYNTAX check, and the mangled file is still syntactically valid bash -- it just means something else. A syntax check cannot see a meaning change. This is the trained-to-be-ignored shape: a check that appears to cover the failure and structurally cannot.
2. **`2>/dev/null` TURNED THE EVIDENCE OFF AND I READ THE SILENCE AS DATA.** My first probe sourced the file with stderr suppressed, got an empty lookup, and I nearly recorded "the rows do not resolve" as a finding about the rows. The two `command not found` lines were the whole diagnosis and I had discarded them in the same command that asked the question.
3. **THE ONLY CONTROL EXISTED BY LUCK.** What exposed it was the PRE-EXISTING `treeindex_commands.bats` row also coming back empty -- a row I had not touched, so its emptiness could not be about my edit. **A table with no existing rows would have taken the corruption silently**, and the next reader would have seen an override table that simply did not override.

## The fix, and the estate already contains it

`view_skew_check.sh` holds its equivalent tables the SAFE way -- a heredoc with a QUOTED delimiter, in which nothing is interpreted:

    UNCHECKABLE="$(cat <<'EOF'    <- safe: no expansion of " or backtick or $
    AUTHORED="$(cat <<'EOF'       <- safe

Two tools in the same directory use the unsafe form:

    lib_classify.sh:208   OVERRIDES="
    lib_classify.sh:290   RATIFICATIONS="
    drift_check.sh:67     EXPLAINED="

**Convert those three to the quoted-heredoc form.** After that a literal `"`, a backtick or a `$` in a note is inert data rather than shell, and the class is closed by construction instead of by everyone remembering to escape.

## Why it matters beyond the typo

These tables hold **human-authored prose explaining classification decisions** -- exactly the content most likely to contain a quotation, because quoting a ruling is the natural way to justify a row. The format is hostile to its own purpose. `OVERRIDES`'s own header says a classification the machine cannot make "is stated by a human, never guessed, because a wrong `retire` is coverage that vanishes at the cut with nobody watching" -- and the mechanism for stating it drops the statement if the human quotes anything.

**Both blocks are currently correct.** This is filed on the mechanism, not on a live corruption; the rows landed after the quotes were escaped and every lookup was driven with positive and negative controls.


=== THE POPULATION IS FOUR, NOT THREE, AND I FOUND THE FOURTH ONLY BY RUNNING THE SWEEP I HAD SKIPPED (cc, 2026-08-31) ===

This issue originally listed three blocks, all under `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/`. **That was the set I had HIT, not the set that EXISTS.** A repo-wide sweep for the form finds a fourth, outside the parity tools entirely:

    intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/lib_classify.sh:208   OVERRIDES="
    intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/lib_classify.sh:290   RATIFICATIONS="
    intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/drift_check.sh:67     EXPLAINED="
    bin/.devbin/lib/builtins:66                          _DEVBIN_BUILTIN_CATALOGUE="

**The fourth carries exactly the content that makes the form dangerous** -- human-authored prose summaries, one per builtin (`Interactive Elixir shell with the project loaded`, `Read-only gates; each exits non-zero on a breach`). It is clean of quotes and backticks today, so nothing is broken; it is the same loaded weapon pointed at the same foot, and it sits in BUILD tooling rather than in the parity harness, so a fix scoped to `parity/tools/` would leave it standing.

**RECORDED AS THIS ISSUE'S OWN INSTANCE OF THE CLASS IT DESCRIBES.** vc named the shape today from two other cases -- `apply_envelopes` carrying general reasoning applied to one narrow field, and `whiteboard-clock-guard.sh` documenting BSD's unspecified-field fill at length while fixing only the date path: **analysis general, patch instance-shaped, and the quality of the writeup is what makes it stop.** This issue was a third instance in the act of describing the second. I wrote the general mechanism, named the general fix, and enumerated only the blocks I had personally tripped over -- then told a peer the population might be larger instead of spending the one grep that settles it.

The sweep is one line and it is recorded here so the next person does not re-derive it:

    grep -rn '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*="$' --include='*.sh' . ; grep -rn '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*="$' bin/ .githooks/

**The second half is load-bearing:** the fourth block is in an EXTENSIONLESS executable, so an `--include='*.sh'` sweep cannot see it. A pattern that cannot match its subject returns the number that means success -- which is the same defect this estate recorded on `disposition == "drop"`, arriving inside the search for this one.
